---
title: "irt_coef"
subtitle: "Stata command for y*-standardized coefficients in item response theory models"
---

`irt_coef` is a Stata command that calculates y\*-standardized coefficients
for binary and ordinal item response theory (IRT) models. The discrimination
parameters of an IRT model are on the log-odds (or probit) scale of each
item, which makes their size hard to judge; standardizing on the latent
propensity y\* behind each item puts the coefficients on a common scale for
interpreting them and for comparing across items and models. The raw
coefficient, its standard error, and *p*-value are reported alongside the
standardized coefficient.

Both types of coefficients are covered in my graduate course slides on
item response theory:
[Item Response Theory slides](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1G9sWGLMAN6SGWzw3XqOXyBw7MC-R_hGI/view?usp=drive_link).
All of the materials for the course, including example code, are on the
[Latent Variable Modeling](https://www.trentonmize.com/teaching/lvm) page.

## Installation

```stata
net install irt_coef, from("https://tdmize.github.io/data") replace
```

To read the help file in Stata, type `help irt_coef`; it is also
[on this site](help.html).

## Citation

Please cite the use of `irt_coef` as:

> Mize, Trenton D. 2024. "irt_coef: Stata command for y*-standardized
> coefficients in item response theory models."
> <https://www.trentonmize.com/software/irt_coef>

## Examples

### After the irt command

The example fits a graded response model to ten ordinal items measuring
mastery (a sense of control over one's life) in Add Health Wave IV.

```{.stata-run}
. use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/lvm_ah4", clear
(Add Health Wave IV | Latent Variable Modeling Class | )

. 
. irt grm nocontrol handle yourway overwhelm nofutureR cantchangeR ///
>         othersdetR interfereR lowcontrolR cantsolveR
```

`irt_coef` then calculates the y*-standardized coefficients. The `help`
option adds a legend beneath the table explaining each column.

```{.stata-run}
. irt_coef, help

y* standardized coefficients (and raw coefficient) from IRT model N=5113

             |   Std Coef        Coef   Std. Err.       P>|z| 
-------------+-----------------------------------------------
   nocontrol |     -0.361      -0.702       0.034       0.000 
      handle |      0.461       0.943       0.037       0.000 
     yourway |      0.459       0.938       0.036       0.000 
   overwhelm |     -0.385      -0.756       0.034       0.000 
   nofutureR |      0.583       1.301       0.043       0.000 
 cantchangeR |      0.732       1.950       0.059       0.000 
  othersdetR |      0.749       2.049       0.063       0.000 
  interfereR |      0.591       1.329       0.042       0.000 
 lowcontrolR |      0.795       2.376       0.070       0.000 
  cantsolveR |      0.815       2.551       0.082       0.000 


Std Coef : y* standardized IRT regression coefficient
Coef     : IRT raw regression coefficient
NOTE     : SE and p-value based on raw regression coefficient

```

### After gsem

An identical model can be fit with `gsem`. Because `gsem` lets the latent
variable take any name, the `latent()` option tells `irt_coef` which one to
use (after `irt` it is always `Theta`, and the option is not needed).

```{.stata-run}
>                  othersdetR interfereR lowcontrolR cantsolveR, ologit), var(Mastery@1)
```

```{.stata-run}
. irt_coef, latent(Mastery)

y* standardized coefficients (and raw coefficient) from IRT model N=5113

             |   Std Coef        Coef   Std. Err.       P>|z| 
-------------+-----------------------------------------------
   nocontrol |      0.361       0.702       0.034       0.000 
      handle |     -0.461      -0.943       0.037       0.000 
     yourway |     -0.459      -0.938       0.036       0.000 
   overwhelm |      0.385       0.756       0.034       0.000 
   nofutureR |     -0.583      -1.301       0.043       0.000 
 cantchangeR |     -0.732      -1.950       0.059       0.000 
  othersdetR |     -0.749      -2.049       0.063       0.000 
  interfereR |     -0.591      -1.329       0.042       0.000 
 lowcontrolR |     -0.795      -2.376       0.070       0.000 
  cantsolveR |     -0.815      -2.551       0.082       0.000 

```

The `sort` option orders the items by the size of the standardized
coefficient, and `decimals()` sets the number of decimal places; see the
[help file](help.html) for the full list of options.
